label: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05

sources.title: SEC staff Compliance and Disclosure Interpretations, Exchange Act Form 8-K, Questions 104B.01 to 104B.09
17 CFR 232.13 (Regulation S-T Rule 13), date of filing, Cornell LII

statusNote: In force since 2023-12-18 (smaller reporting companies since 2024-06-15). The Attorney General may delay disclosure for national security or public safety.

triggers.label: Incident discovered
triggers.hint: The materiality determination must follow without unreasonable delay.

triggers.label: Materiality determined
triggers.hint: Players (with counsel) decide the incident is material. The 4 business days start here.

triggers.label: Attorney General delay ended
triggers.hint: Only if the Attorney General determined that disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety. Requesting a delay does not change the duty; the four business days run from the end of the delay (staff interpretations 104B.02 and 104B.03). Confirm the reading with counsel.

clocks.label: Form 8-K Item 1.05
clocks.rule: File within four business days after determining the incident is material. EDGAR dates a Form 8-K submitted after 5:30 p.m. Eastern as filed the next business day (Regulation S-T Rule 13(a)(2)), so the real deadline is 5:30 p.m. Eastern on the fourth business day; this clock shows the time of day of the determination. Information not determined or unavailable at filing goes in an 8-K/A within four business days after it is known.

clocks.label: Form 8-K Item 1.05 after an Attorney General delay
clocks.rule: Use this clock instead of the first one only when the Attorney General delayed disclosure. File within four business days after the delay ends.

appliesTo.note: Public companies that file with the SEC.
